pull.title: fix(runtime): retain safe prerequisite launch diagnostics
pull.body:
Helper startup currently reports the same Aspire “missing” diagnostic for a missing executable, denied execute permission and an executable held open for writing. Retain a finite failure kind and native error code through HXR015 so these refusals are distinguishable, while preserving fail-closed behavior, output bounds and existing deadlines. Exception text, paths, arguments and environment values are excluded from the new metadata.

The branch also retains the original reviewed guard commits from PR162 in its ancestry. Their content is already on restored main; normal merge through this PR integrates that history after the external rollback and restoration recorded in the earlier PR description.

Validation: all27 focused cases pass, including all19 original cases. Three actual filesystem regressions fail before the fix and in a compiled metadata-omission copy, then pass with the correction. The normal Release rebuild has zero warnings/errors. All12 restored Hexalith package archives passed normal repository-signature verification; actual public output bodies were matched to their signed members. Required hosted CI and merged-main validation remain required. The original hosted native launch error is still unproved.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes affect G-4 package publication and release source gates plus composition prerequisite diagnostics; behavior is fail-closed with expanded tests but touches security-sensitive release paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Helper process startup** now records bounded launch-failure metadata (`CompositionProcessStartFailure` kind and optional native error code) on `CompositionProcessResult` instead of treating every failed start as a generic “missing” case. **Aspire prerequisite HXR015** messages incorporate that metadata so missing, permission-denied, and locked executables are distinguishable without echoing paths, arguments, or exception text.
> 
> **G-4 release source verification** is tightened in the same branch: `Assert-CurrentReleaseSource` still skips GitHub for local executed qualification, but in the **release** job it requires the full protected workflow context and always runs the live branch-tip guard (CI run proof env vars only when validation mode is `ci`). **`verify-g4-release-source.sh`** validates the entire Git ref API payload, not just the tip SHA. Shell and PowerShell regression suites cover malformed refs, legacy executed-mode publication, and publisher late-guard expectations.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c354a044e40d70f494732180be0046611bae44cf. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
